name: Partner-Resisted Straight Punch Hold
definition: A unilateral standing isometric straight-punch hold against a partner's rearward manual pressure. The boxer plants a comfortable boxing stance and holds the working fist near full straight-punch reach at roughly shoulder height while the partner presses back along the punch line; the opposite hand stays at guard. The Boxing Science library specifies partner resistance, near-full jab range, and 5-10-second holds, but not measured force, exact joint angles, or a mandatory lead/rear arm. The stance, fist height, partner hand-to-fist contact, and rearward pressure direction are bounded catalog choices to make one repeatable straight-line fixture. An active punch, changing-angle sequence, hook, uppercut, landmine punch, wall press, or partner perturbation hold is outside this family. Manual resistance is represented as bodyweight/nonComparable to avoid a false weight field; the required partner is explicit in the name and instructions. Anterior deltoid and clavicular pectoralis share non-ranked primary shoulder credit; the remaining roles are conservative anatomy-and-mechanics inferences, not EMG rankings measured in this hold.

variantAxes.description: Stable stance selected for the straight-punch hold.
Held straight-punch position near full reach, with the fist around shoulder height.
Partner contact and resistance direction during the stationary hold.
Partner hand contact at the working fist, not the forearm or elbow.
One arm works per logged hold; repeat on the other side in a separate hold.
The partner opposes a static fist position without a rail, lever, or guided load path.

execution.startingPosition: Stand in a stable boxing stance with a partner facing you. Bring one fist toward near-full straight-punch reach at about shoulder height, and keep the other hand at guard. Have the partner place their palm against the working fist.
execution.movement: Press forward into the partner while they apply steady pressure directly back along the straight punch line. Keep the fist almost still rather than throwing a punch.
execution.endpoint: Hold the same near-full-reach position for 5-10 seconds, then release. Train the other arm in a separate hold.
execution.controlledJoints: Keep the working shoulder and elbow near their starting angles; do not repeatedly bend or extend the arm.
execution.supportAndPosture: Keep both feet planted and the trunk and pelvis controlled. Ask the partner to maintain smooth resistance rather than jerking the arm.
execution.sideOrDirection: Record one timed hold for one working arm; repeat on the other side separately.
disqualifyingCompensations: Throwing the fist forward or letting it recoil turns the hold into a dynamic punch.
Bending the elbow across the chest changes the position to a hook hold.
Driving upward from a lowered fist changes the position to an uppercut hold.
Using a wall or landmine changes the resistance geometry.
